findings.name: Ad Valorem (Homestead) Tax Exemption for Totally Disabled Veterans
findings.description: Mississippi veterans with a service-connected total disability rating, who were honorably discharged, are exempt from ad valorem (homestead property) taxes on their residence. The exemption extends to the un-remarried surviving spouse of a qualifying veteran. The exemption applies to the homestead property in Mississippi where the veteran resides.
findings.value: Full exemption from ad valorem taxes on homestead property
otherReqs: Service-connected total disability rating from the VA
Un-remarried surviving spouses of qualifying veterans also covered
findings.agency: Mississippi Veterans Affairs / County Tax Assessor
documentation: VA disability rating letter confirming total service-connected disability
DD-214 or proof of honorable discharge
findings.sourceExcerpt: Ad Valorem Tax Exemption - Service-connected total disability Veterans exempt from homestead property taxes; unmarried surviving spouses also covered. (Miss. Code Ann. §27-33-75, §27-33-67)

findings.name: 100% Disabled Veteran License Plate ($1 Annual Fee)
findings.description: Mississippi veterans rated 100% permanent service-connected disabled, or at least 70% nonpermanent service-connected disabled, by the VA may purchase up to two motor vehicle/pickup license plates or one motorcycle license plate for $1 each annually. Vehicles registered with a disabled veteran plate are exempt from all ad valorem and privilege taxes. Veterans with a nonpermanent 70%+ rating must provide an updated VA benefits letter at each renewal. Applications are made in person at the county Tax Collector's office.
findings.value: $1 annual fee per plate (up to 2 vehicle plates or 1 motorcycle plate); exempt from ad valorem and privilege taxes
otherReqs: 100% permanent service-connected disability, OR at least 70% nonpermanent service-connected disability
Nonpermanent 70%+ rating requires an updated VA benefits letter at each renewal
Apply in person at the county Tax Collector's office
findings.agency: Mississippi Department of Revenue / County Tax Collector
findings.sourceExcerpt: Discounted License Plates - 100% permanent service-connected disabled Veterans: $1 annually for one motor vehicle/pickup or one motorcycle. (Miss. Code Ann. §27-19-53, §27-19-31)

findings.name: Hunting/Fishing License Exemption for Totally Disabled Veterans
findings.description: Mississippi veterans with a total service-connected disability are exempt from purchasing hunting and fishing licenses, but must carry proof of age, residency, and disability status while hunting or fishing.
findings.value: Exempt from hunting and fishing license fees
otherReqs: Must carry proof of age, residency, and disability status while hunting or fishing
findings.agency: Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks
documentation: VA disability rating letter confirming total service-connected disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: Hunting/Fishing License Exemption - Total service-connected disability Veterans exempt from licenses but must carry proof of age, residency, and disability. (Miss. Code Ann. §49-7-5)

findings.name: In-State Tuition for Veterans Using Title 38 Education Benefits
findings.description: Any veteran, or person entitled to education benefits under Title 38 of the U.S. Code (e.g., the GI Bill), is authorized to receive in-state tuition rates at Mississippi public colleges and universities regardless of formal state residency.
findings.value: In-state tuition rate regardless of formal residency
otherReqs: Must be entitled to federal Title 38 education benefits
documentation: VA Certificate of Eligibility for Title 38 education benefits
findings.sourceExcerpt: In-State Tuition - Any Veteran or person entitled to education benefits under Title 38 U.S. Code is authorized in-state tuition. (Miss. Code Ann. §37-103-25)

findings.name: Educational Scholarship for Children of POW/MIA Service Members
findings.description: Children of prisoner-of-war or missing-in-action service members receive an eight-semester scholarship (not including the cost of books and fees) at Mississippi state colleges and universities.
findings.value: Eight-semester scholarship covering tuition (excluding books/fees) at Mississippi state colleges and universities
otherReqs: Applicant must be a dependent child of a POW or MIA service member
findings.sourceExcerpt: Educational Assistance for Dependents - Children of POW/MIA service members receive eight-semester scholarships (excluding books/fees) at state colleges/universities. (Miss. Code Ann. §37-108-1)

findings.name: State Employment Veterans' Preference
findings.description: The Mississippi State Personnel Board lists disabled veterans and veterans at the top of eligible applicant lists for state jobs, with disabled veterans listed before non-disabled veterans. All applicants must indicate veteran status on their state job application. During a layoff, veterans and disabled veterans are granted retention preference over non-veteran employees. Under Senate Bill 2863 (2019), the statutory definitions of "veteran" and "disabled veteran" were updated to align with federal standards, and Purple Heart recipients now qualify as disabled veterans for preference purposes.
findings.value: Top-of-list hiring preference for state jobs (disabled veterans ranked ahead of veterans); retention preference during layoffs
otherReqs: Must indicate veteran status on state job application
Disabled veteran status requires meeting federal disability standards or Purple Heart recipient status
documentation: DD-214 or proof of military service
VA disability rating letter (for disabled veteran preference tier)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Disabled veterans and veterans are listed at the top of the list with disabled veterans listed before veterans. Disabled Veterans: Individuals meeting federal disability standards, plus Purple Heart recipients (newly qualified under SB 2863). All applicants must indicate veteran status on their applications.

findings.name: Mississippi State Veterans Homes
findings.description: Mississippi operates five state veterans homes — in Collins, Jackson, Kosciusko, Oxford, and Tradition (Biloxi) — serving approximately 600 veterans with long-term nursing care, medical services, and rehabilitation. Admission requires the applicant to have served on active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces without a dishonorable discharge (or be the spouse of a current resident), to be or have been a Mississippi resident (non-residents may be admitted absent a waiting resident), and to pass a physician examination within 30 days of admission. The homes are governed by the Mississippi Veterans Affairs Board, a seven-member board appointed by the Governor.
findings.value: Long-term nursing care, medical services, and rehabilitation at five state veterans homes
otherReqs: Active duty service without dishonorable discharge (DD-214 required), or be the spouse of a current resident
Mississippi residency required (or have been a MS resident); non-residents admitted only if no MS resident is waiting
Must pass a physician examination within 30 days of admission
findings.form: Application for Admission to a Mississippi Veterans Home
findings.sourceExcerpt: Mississippi operates five veterans homes across the state: Collins, Jackson, Kosciusko, Oxford, and Tradition. Applicants must have been active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces and must not have been discharged under dishonorable conditions, be or have been a Mississippi resident, and pass a physician examination within 30 days of admission.
